key_insight: Temperature-dependent Raman and XRD disentangle two distinct structural events in SrLaCoNbO6: a low-temperature isostructural octahedral distortion near 300 ± 25 °C and a high-temperature symmetry-breaking transition near 750 ± 25 °C.
engineering_relevance: The study shows that lab-based Raman plus XRD can reliably monitor perovskite structure stability and phase evolution, which is useful for designing thermally robust oxide materials and device-relevant ceramics.
method: Raman spectroscopy from 25–900 °C to track phonon shifts and linewidth changes.
Laboratory XRD to follow reflection evolution and phase symmetry changes.
Quantitative octahedral distortion analysis plus group-theoretical/Rietveld refinement.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports two temperature anomalies with pronounced phonon renormalization and XRD reflection suppression, supporting assignment of octahedral distortion and a phase transition.
watch_item: Interpretation relies on temperature-dependent structural probes and refinement models, so subtle intermediate phases or composition-dependent effects may be missed without complementary in situ techniques.
paper_title: Disentangling octahedral distortion and symmetry breaking in the ordered double perovskite SrLaCoNbO$_6$
